runs.rationale_summary: The agent stopped on LimitsExceeded after 50 calls without submitting. defects4j failed (Perl String::Interpolate missing) and mvn was absent, so it simulated the chain in a /tmp Java program and got 112.5. Its notes say 'BUG: Should be (point2.X - point1.X ...)' in drift and call nudge 'correct', even though it had the full nudge body. Its drift grep covered only source/, so it never found testDrift.

The harness labels this run provider_error, but the agent caused it. A malformed grep, grep -rn "(\|at) \*", dumped 1.8 MB, and the next request failed with ContextWindowExceededError (643,678 tokens > 200k). The agent had read the whole chain, including apply's fault line. Its notes listed 'BitField.wordOffset (incorrect formula causes premature rejection)' first and apply second. That reading gets the guard wrong: the guard tests < 0, and the agent read 256 >= 64 as a rejection.

The agent followed the registry correctly: it read Packers.forSource (int[] -> Packer32) and then printed Packer32.pack, fault line (i + holderPos) * 32 included, at step 26. It spent the remaining calls re-reading Packer16/8/4/1 and the sibling Conversion methods. It hit LimitsExceeded at 50 calls without committing to a ranking. The test harness was broken (defects4j Perl error, no mvn).

The guard padding cut off the grep -A20 output, so the agent used sed to print the full resolve body, dx = d.getX() * f included. Its evidence chain still says 'Test expects x=87.5 = 100 + 0.25*(50-100), so the offset should be point2 - point1. drift has the sign reversed'. It submitted after 7 calls without running the test or looking at testDrift.

The agent read the whole chain with greps, including the full nudge body. It hand-computed x = 112.5 and concluded 'The test expects 87.5, which needs point2 - point1 ... The drift direction is reversed'. It said itself that the failing test was not run. It made no search over tests/, so it never saw testDrift.

This is the runner variant, so the prompt carried only the defects4j header ('Failing tests: 1'). The agent made the same 7 greps as the opus55 runs and printed the nudge body. Its inference was 'drift subtracts in the wrong order, so the sign is flipped and the slice moves the wrong way'. It ran no test and did no test-side search, so it never reached the testDrift pin.

The agent stopped on LimitsExceeded after 50 calls. It had read the full resolve body twice. Because defects4j was broken, it simulated the chain in /tmp Java with 'drift_buggy' vs 'drift_fixed' (point2 - point1) and confirmed that the drift-reversal fix reproduces 87.5. It then spent its last ~15 calls checking package names. It never searched tests/.

This is a real 300 s timeout: the agent was making tool calls until about 298 s, 49 calls in all. It confirmed with a /tmp simulation that a 'reversed drift' gives 87.5, which made drift its working suspect. It then spent about 25 calls trying to build and run the test itself, after defects4j failed on the missing Perl module (ant compile -source 1.4, javac -source 6, find over /Users). It never searched tests/ for drift.

Its attempts to run the test failed (defects4j Perl error, ant compile error). Its Python simulation then showed that 'drift = point2 - point1' gives 87.5. Its evidence chain says drift 'should compute point2-point1 (exploded - unexploded) to move sections outward. This is the primary bug.' Its caller greps (.drift(, .nudge() covered only source/, so testDrift was missed. It ranked the shallower hops rim, ring and getArcBounds above nudge.

This is probably a provider stall. The last tool output came at about 197 s, followed by about 103 s of silence until the 300 s timeout, against a normal 2-5 s gap between calls. The agent had 10 calls left. It had read widen's unmasked words[i] = run[i] and simulated the negative word ('sign-extended!', 0xFFFFCDF1F0C1DEF0 vs expected). Its simulation comment also tagged overlay's unmasked OR as 'CURRENT BUGGY CODE', so it had not yet settled between widen and overlay. It also ran git log, which showed the outer harness repo, and searched for mvn.

The request hung. The agent made 20 calls in the first 56 s, read the whole chain including apply's p = (i + a) * n and widen's wordOffset guard, and attempted defects4j (Perl error) and mvn (not found). After that there was about 245 s of silence until the 300 s timeout. No hypothesis was recorded before the stall.

The request hung. The agent made 15 calls in about 48 s, read the chain top-down including compose's unpositioned field = (1L << width) - 1 and overlay, and attempted defects4j and mvn, both broken. Then it went silent for about 250 s until the timeout. It had not yet looked for overlay's second caller, BitField.setValue.

The agent found the decisive second caller, BitField.setValue -> overlay(..., _mask), and its own simulation printed 'BitField.setValue is not affected ... (because field IS already the positioned mask)'. It still concluded that 'overlay is buggy when field doesn't match position' and that in setValue 'the bug in overlay happens to cancel out'. It ranked the chain in strict depth order (overlay, combine, widen, compose). overlay is a declared decoy; it is labelled DEFINER here because it owns the positioned-field convention.

The request hung. The agent made 17 calls in about 49 s, read every hop including overlay's shift = (index + at) * width, and attempted defects4j and mvn, both broken. Then it went silent for about 250 s until the timeout. This matches the 'hung requests excluded' note on the control.

In the runner setup defects4j worked; with tail -30 the trigger run showed only 'Failing tests: 1'. At step 92 the agent ran grep -rn over tests/ and found PlotUtilitiesTests.testDrift. It reasoned that drift matches testDrift, so 'The bug is in Plot.nudge(): it should subtract drift * explodePercent, not add', and ran testDrift ('Failing tests: 0'). It then hit LimitsExceeded at 50 calls before submitting. This is the only run in this chunk that held the gold hypothesis.

pattern:
Chunk 1/6 covers 15 runs: 4 wrong answers, 6 that ran out of steps or context, 1 genuine timeout and 4 provider stalls.

Chart definer/composite runs (8): the model always found and read the gold adapter in full (Plot.nudge or Plot.resolve). Every run that formed a hypothesis without the pin blamed PlotUtilities.drift: 'subtraction reversed', 'should be point2 - point1'. All 3 Opus answers had rank 1 = drift, with gold at 3, 3 and 2. Opus used 7 calls, ran no test and searched no tests. The Sonnet answer had gold at rank 5, behind the shallower hops. So the failure is attribution, not search: a convention prior (drift 'should' be exploded minus unexploded) plus never fetching the testDrift pin. Every caller grep was limited to source/. The one exception, sonnet46t run-002, grepped tests/, found testDrift, ran it (it passes) and switched to nudge, but used up its 50 calls before submitting.

Lang runs (7): 4 Sonnet runs (LEX-013, MASK-006, CONV-LONG-003, DEPTH-003) are provider stalls. Each went silent for 100-250 s after its last tool output, and each had already read the gold body. The 2 Haiku runs ran out of steps or context: REGISTRY navigated the registry to Packer32 and then drifted, and LEX overflowed its own context with a malformed grep (the harness labels it provider_error). The one answered Lang miss (MASK-012) is an evidence-integration failure. It found the decisive second caller, BitField.setValue, and simulated that overlay is correct for a positioned mask. It then still blamed overlay and ranked the chain in strict depth order.

Across the chunk:
- In the haiku45, sonnet46 and opus55 directories, defects4j was broken (missing Perl String::Interpolate) and mvn was absent. Agents replaced the test with ad hoc /tmp Java or Python simulations. In the opus55t/sonnet46t runner directories defects4j worked, but the output only said 'Failing tests: N'.
- No run in this chunk ever saw real assertion failure values.
- The gold was exposed and fully read in all 15 runs.

Field conventions: external_evidence_integrated is null when the evidence was not retrieved. The MASK overlay is labelled DEFINER because it owns the field-position convention, although it is also a declared decoy.
